# kkguai

> kkguai is a free, open-source RemoteApp (RDP) client for macOS. It connects to a Windows 10/11 Pro PC you already own and turns individual Windows programs into native Mac windows — one window and one Dock icon per app, with no virtual machine, no full remote desktop, and no Parallels subscription.

> kkguai 是一款免费开源的 macOS RemoteApp 客户端。它连接已有的 Windows 10/11 专业版电脑，把每个 Windows 程序变成 Mac 上的原生窗口：一个程序一个窗口、一个 Dock 图标。不需要虚拟机，不需要整块远程桌面，也不需要 Parallels 订阅。

- Version: 0.2.9 (2026-11-23)
- License: MIT
- Price: free
- Platform: macOS 14 or later, Apple Silicon
- Host: Windows 10/11 Pro (or Enterprise / Windows Server) with Remote Desktop enabled
- Network: LAN, VPN, or Tailscale
- Source: https://github.com/kkguai666/kkguai
- Download: https://github.com/kkguai666/kkguai/releases/latest
- Website (Chinese): https://kkguai666.github.io/kkguai/
- Website (English): https://kkguai666.github.io/kkguai/en/

## What it does

- Runs one native macOS window per remote Windows program (RemoteApp), instead of streaming a whole desktop.
- Retina rendering: 200% session scaling, 2x pixel rendering, 1/2-point coordinate mapping.
- Mac input methods for Chinese, Japanese and Korean; composed on the Mac and sent as Unicode.
- Remote cursor shapes and hotspots; local window drag and resize; multi-monitor layout mirroring.
- One Dock icon per remote app, Windows 11-style Start menu, Spotlight and Launchpad support.
- Interface localized into Chinese (Simplified), English, Japanese and Korean, following the Mac's preferred languages.
- Connection watchdog with menu bar state and one-click reconnect; per-host window layout memory; fill screen, keep on top and move a window to the next display.
- Saved Windows PCs plus discovery on the LAN and on Tailscale; bidirectional text clipboard.
- Global hotkeys: Option-Space opens a command palette for apps, commands and workspaces; Option-` cycles remote windows.
- Named workspaces reopen a whole set of apps in their saved positions.
- In-app updater and an in-app feedback form that can attach a diagnostics bundle.

## How it compares

- Parallels Desktop: runs a full Windows virtual machine on the Mac, requires a subscription (from $99/year) and a Windows licence. kkguai uses a Windows PC you already own, is free, and does not use the Mac's RAM or CPU for Windows.
- Microsoft Windows App (Remote Desktop): free, but shows the entire Windows desktop in one window. RemoteApp support in Microsoft's client requires enterprise AVD/RDS infrastructure.
- UTM: a virtual machine app; requires a Windows licence and VM resources.
- kkguai's trade-off: the Windows host must stay on and reachable; Windows Home cannot host RDP.

## Install (summary)

1. On Windows 10/11 Pro, enable Remote Desktop and allow it through the firewall.
2. Import `enable-remoteapp.reg` from the release as administrator (required), optionally `single-session.reg`, then reboot.
3. On the Mac, download `kkguai-0.2.9-macos-arm64.dmg`, drag kkguai into Applications.
4. Before first launch: `xattr -dr com.apple.quarantine /Applications/kkguai.app` (the build is not notarized yet).

## Limitations

- Apple Silicon only in the current release; Intel Macs must build from source.
- Not notarized by Apple; one xattr command is required on first launch.
- Windows Home cannot host RDP.
- The remote Windows PC must remain on and reachable.
- If the same Windows account is already signed in to a desktop session, app-window mode cannot connect; sign that session out first.
